findings.title: `AssignmentSource.queued` default is evaluated once at import time
findings.body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` on the `AssignmentSource` dataclass evaluates `timezone.now()` once when the module is imported rather than when each instance is created. As a result, every `AssignmentSource` instantiated without an explicit `queued` argument will carry the timestamp of when the worker process started. Use `dataclasses.field(default_factory=timezone.now)` so the timestamp is generated per instance.

findings.title: `assignment_source` added to `sync_status_outbound` instead of `sync_assignee_outbound`
findings.body: `assignment_source: AssignmentSource | None = None` was added to `IssueSyncIntegration.sync_status_outbound`, which syncs resolution status and is never called with an `assignment_source`. Meanwhile, `src/sentry/integrations/tasks/sync_assignee_outbound.py` (line 60) passes `assignment_source=parsed_assignment_source` to `installation.sync_assignee_outbound`, whose signature on `IssueSyncIntegration` was not updated (and any subclass implementation of `sync_assignee_outbound` that does not accept `**kwargs` will raise `TypeError`). Either move the parameter to `sync_assignee_outbound` or omit it from the `installation.sync_assignee_outbound` call since the cycle check already happens in `installation.should_sync`.
